mode: READ-ONLY analysis lane (no writes, no git, no deploy)
missionPremise: Stripe on cortex-api is TEST mode and live activation is deliberately deferred to the operator (established in dispatch, sourced to _decisions/2026-08-24_stripe_annual_pricing_and_live_activation.md). The lane produces the exact ordered activation checklist, derived from the write path in legacy-design-tools origin/main, with a verification for every step and an explicit silent-failure section, because a wrong-mode Stripe value does not raise at deploy time and several of them take money without granting anything.
completionPredicate: A stranger holding this close can execute the switch top to bottom, and for every step can name (a) the command or dashboard action, (b) who performs it, and (c) a check that fails when the step did not work. Every code claim carries file:line on a named commit. Claims that could not be established from code are listed as unestablished rather than guessed.
scopeBasis: Scoped to what must CHANGE or be CONFIGURED for live, plus what BREAKS at the test-to-live boundary. Excluded deliberately: performing the switch (operator-owned, explicitly out of scope), pricing-ladder relitigation (LOCKED 2026-08-10 / 2026-08-24), and Stripe dashboard onboarding mechanics that leave no trace in this repo. Included beyond the literal ask: hauska-map apps/property-explorer, because the PE client is where the retired-price-id fallback lives and item 6 cannot be answered from legacy-design-tools alone.

item2_webhookSecretIsAThirdSwap.path: artifacts/api-server/src/lib/brokerageStripe.ts:368 reads STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET; :372-374 refuses when absent; :385 passes it to parseStripeEvent; :739-750 HMAC-SHA256 over `${t}.${rawBody}` compared timing-safe against every v1= part; mismatch throws; :386-389 maps the throw to handled:false invalid_signature; routes/brokerageBilling.ts:186-189 turns any unhandled result into HTTP 400.
item2_webhookSecretIsAThirdSwap.why: Stripe issues a distinct whsec_ per endpoint object, and live-mode endpoints are separate objects from test-mode endpoints. Keeping the test whsec_ makes every live event fail the HMAC, so every live payment is collected by Stripe and grants nothing.

item3_webhookEventTypes.everythingElse: artifacts/api-server/src/lib/brokerageStripe.ts:592 returns handled:false reason=ignored_event_type:<type>, which routes/brokerageBilling.ts:186-189 serves as HTTP 400
item3_webhookEventTypes.consequence: Subscribing the live endpoint to any FOURTH type (or to 'all events') produces a 400 on every extra delivery. Stripe counts those as endpoint failures, alerts, and can disable the endpoint — taking the three real types down with it. Configure EXACTLY these three.
item3_webhookEventTypes.namedHazard: checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded is NOT handled. If any delayed-settlement payment method (ACH / bank debit / deferred Link) is enabled in live mode, that path collects money and never grants.

item4_otherLiveChanges.apiVersionPin: NONE. VERIFIED by repo-wide grep: no Stripe-Version header, no api_version anywhere in artifacts/ or scripts/. Both call sites (brokerageStripe.ts:129-136 and :651-653) send only Authorization. The account's dashboard default API version governs, and it can change under the code without a deploy.
item4_otherLiveChanges.automaticTax: ABSENT. VERIFIED: no automatic_tax, no customer_update, no billing_address_collection, no tax_id anywhere. Enabling Stripe Tax is a CODE change, not a dashboard-only switch.
item4_otherLiveChanges.idempotency: ABSENT. VERIFIED: no Idempotency-Key header on any Stripe POST. Webhook replays are mostly harmless because createPePropertyUnlock upserts (peEntitlement.ts:218-238) and setPeAccessTierFromStripe is a full-row update (peIdentity.ts:234-246).
item4_otherLiveChanges.promotionCodes: allow_promotion_codes=true is set on the PE SUBSCRIPTION path only (pePaywallStripe.ts:378). NOT set on the $15 unlock (mode=payment, pePaywallStripe.ts:472-480) and NOT on the install-scoped brokerage checkout (brokerageStripe.ts:191-203). Coupons and promotion codes are mode-scoped in Stripe: every test-mode code must be recreated in live, and any live code that exists is redeemable by anyone holding it. A discount is detected at brokerageStripe.ts:354-362 and recorded as entitlement_source=stripe_promo.
item4_otherLiveChanges.customerPortal: createBillingPortalSession (brokerageStripe.ts:228-254) is called from exactly ONE route, POST /api/brokerage/v1/billing/portal (brokerageBilling.ts:109), which is install-scoped and brokerageAuth-gated. VERIFIED: the PE app in hauska-map never calls it (no billing/portal, billing_portal or portalUrl reference under apps/property-explorer). Stripe requires a portal configuration per mode; live mode has none until created, and the error surfaces as 502 portal_failed.
item4_otherLiveChanges.successCancelUrls: MIXED. Server defaults are env-derived with HARDCODED fallbacks: pePaywallStripe.ts:126-129 (PE_WEB_APP_BASE_URL -> https://property-explorer-xi.vercel.app) and brokerageBillingUrls.ts:4-7 (BROKERAGE_BILLING_PUBLIC_BASE_URL -> https://cortex-api-tds7av26va-uc.a.run.app). Both env vars are VERIFIED ABSENT on the serving revision, and neither is in the workflow's authoritative-replace --set-env-vars, so they cannot be hand-set durably. The PE client overrides both from window.location.origin (billingClient.ts:50-62) so real users land back on the host they started from; its non-browser fallback https://property-explorer.vercel.app is a VERIFIED DEAD host (404).
item4_otherLiveChanges.publishableKeyDistribution: GOOD NEWS: there is no hardcoded pk_ anywhere in the PE app. The key travels from cortex-api env to the client on the checkout response and into loadStripe (stripeCheckoutMount.ts:87-88). Swapping the STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY secret flips the browser with no PE redeploy.
item4_otherLiveChanges.csp: apps/property-explorer/vercel.json already allows js.stripe.com, *.stripe.com and hooks.stripe.com in script-src and frame-src. No CSP change needed for live.

peSide.storedField: pe_user_entitlements.stripe_customer_id (lib/db/src/schema/peUserEntitlements.ts:60). NO subscription id is stored on the PE side.
peSide.behaviour: getOrCreatePeStripeCustomer (pePaywallStripe.ts:246-251) returns the stored id unconditionally and passes it as `customer:` to /checkout/sessions (pePaywallStripe.ts:376). Under a live key a test cus_ produces Stripe 400 'No such customer', stripePostForm throws (brokerageStripe.ts:140-145), and the route returns 502 checkout_failed carrying the raw Stripe message (propertyExplorer.ts:1275-1279).
peSide.verdict: LOUD but PERMANENTLY BLOCKING and self-deadlocking. There is no catch that clears the stale id and retries. setPeAccessTierFromStripe would overwrite it (peIdentity.ts:241-243) but only on a SUCCESSFUL checkout, which the stale id prevents. Every pre-cutover PE user who ever opened a checkout is locked out of paying until the column is cleared. The raw Stripe error also leaks a customer id into the end-user UI.

brokerageSide.behaviour: getOrCreateStripeCustomer (brokerageStripe.ts:149-151) has the same shape. On the PORTAL route the 'No such customer' error is caught and mapped to 404 no_billing_customer with the message 'No Stripe customer for this install — complete checkout first' (brokerageBilling.ts:116-121), which is WRONG: the customer exists, in the other mode. A misdiagnosing message, not a fix.
brokerageSide.subscriptionIds: installIdFromStripeSubscription (brokerageStripe.ts:706-722) falls back to a lookup by stripe_subscription_id. Live subscriptions carry metadata.install_id so the fallback is not normally reached; a stale test id in that column simply never matches a live event.

item5_staleTestModeIds.testModeEventsAfterCutover: Test-mode events are delivered only to test-mode endpoints. If the existing test endpoint stays pointed at production, every test event will now fail the live whsec_ and return 400 — noisy but fail-closed. Disable or delete the test endpoint as part of the cutover.

item6_retiredPricePair.verdict: REFUTED as an operational claim; TRUE only as a statement about pePaywallStripe.ts
item6_retiredPricePair.commentUnderTest: artifacts/api-server/src/lib/pePaywallStripe.ts:23-26 — 'The retired STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID / STRIPE_MAX_PRICE_ID pair is never read here ... and remains only in the install-scoped brokerage extension seam.'
item6_retiredPricePair.whatIsTrue: Neither name is read in pePaywallStripe.ts. On the WEBHOOK, the PE branches return before the install-scoped branches, so resolveSubscriptionTierFromStripe -> tierFromStripeObject -> subscriptionTierFromPriceId is genuinely unreachable from a PE grant (brokerageStripe.ts:436-479 returns before :481; :505-538 returns before :541).
item6_retiredPricePair.whatIsFalse: The pair IS reached from a live PE surface, twice over:
item6_retiredPricePair.path1: hauska-map apps/property-explorer/src/lib/billingClient.ts:103-106 — if the user-scoped route POST /api/property-explorer/v1/billing/checkout returns 403 or 404, the SHIPPED PE client falls back to startPeCheckoutInstallScoped, which at billingClient.ts:144-148 posts a body with a HARDCODED tier:'pro' and NO tier/interval/seats from the user's click, to /brokerage/v1/property-explorer/billing/checkout -> propertyExplorerBilling.ts:70 -> createSubscriptionCheckoutSession -> stripePriceIdForTier -> STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID. A Studio, Team or annual click therefore opens a checkout at the pre-ladder Pro price. This is exactly the defect class pePaywallStripe.ts:360-363 says was fixed, reintroduced one layer up in the client.
item6_retiredPricePair.path2: hauska-map apps/property-explorer/api/pe-billing.ts:50 is a DEPLOYED Vercel function, routed in vercel.json:42, that proxies POST /api/pe-billing?path=checkout straight to the same install-scoped seam. Nothing in apps/property-explorer/src references it, but it is publicly routable on the production host and creates a real Stripe subscription checkout at STRIPE_PRO_PRICE_ID.
item6_retiredPricePair.secondMechanismConsidered: Alternative explanation for the fallback existing: it is dead code that can never fire, because requirePeAuthenticated returns 401 (not 403/404) and the Vercel deep-proxy allowlist contains 'api/property-explorer/v1/billing/checkout' (apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/deep-allowlist.ts:51). Rejected as a safety argument, not as a description: the fallback fires on any condition that makes the route 404 or 403 — a cortex-api revision without the route, a proxy or allowlist regression, a rewrite change — and none of those are prevented by anything. The correct reading is 'currently not firing', not 'cannot fire'. It is one deploy accident away from charging live money at the wrong price.

lesson: A price id is a bearer of an AMOUNT and an INTERVAL, and this code validates neither. Fail-closed on absence (PeCheckoutConfigError) is real and well built; there is no check at all on a present-but-wrong value. Absence is handled, wrongness is not — that asymmetry is the whole shape of the Stripe cutover risk.

The webhook route turns EVERY unhandled result into HTTP 400, including the benign ignored_event_type. That makes the live endpoint's event-type subscription list a load-bearing configuration item: one extra subscribed type generates continuous 400s that Stripe reads as endpoint failure.

'Never read on a live PE path' was true of the file it was written in and false of the product. A negative-reachability claim scoped to one file is not a claim about the system; the client repo held the counterexample.
propertyExplorerBilling.ts is named for Property Explorer and is entirely the install-scoped legacy seam. Naming is not architecture — the user-scoped PE checkout lives in propertyExplorer.ts:1230.
